name: Wyoming
overview: Wyoming offers an income- and asset-tested homeowner tax refund alongside value exemptions introduced or expanded for 2025.

programs.name: Property Tax Refund Program
programs.incomeDefinition: Total household income compared with the greater of county or state median household income.
programs.incomeLimits: Up to 145% of applicable median income, with lower benefits above the 125% tier.
programs.maximumBenefit: 75% of eligible taxes paid, limited to half the county median residential tax bill; upper income tier receives a 35% reduction.
programs.formulaSummary: Income-tier refund using paid taxes, county median tax cap and asset/residency tests.
programs.application: Annual application through Department of Revenue or official refund portal; supporting tax-payment and household-income records required.
eligibilityNotes: Wyoming resident at least five years; primary residence.
2025 refund portal lists asset limit below $169,866 per adult, with program exclusions.

sources.title: Wyoming Property Tax Refund System: 2025 refunds

programs.name: Homeowner Property Tax Exemption
programs.maximumBenefit: 25% of the first $1 million of qualifying residence and improved-land fair market value.
programs.formulaSummary: Value exemption introduced for tax year 2025; owner-occupancy limitation applies beginning in 2026.
programs.application: 2025 application treatment differs from owner-occupancy applications in later years; consult county assessor.
interactions: Cannot combine with long-term homeowner exemption for 2025/26.

programs.name: Long-term Homeowner Exemption
programs.ageRule: Owner or spouse age 65 or older.
programs.formulaSummary: Primary-residence exemption for owner/spouse with at least 25 years paying Wyoming residential property tax.
programs.application: Claim through local assessor under statutory process.
eligibilityNotes: Effective January 1, 2025; original legislation sunsets July 1, 2027.

sources.title: Wyoming HB0003 enacted long-term homeowner exemption

laterChanges: 25% homeowner value exemption becomes limited to owner-occupied property beginning in 2026.
researchNotes: County median-income and median-tax-bill tables are required to calculate an exact refund.
The 25% and 50% exemptions are not additive in 2025/26.
